events.title: Bryant Park Picnic Performance: Asian American Arts Alliance: Grace Kelly, Ashni
events.description: Grace Kelly is a saxophonist, singer, songwriter, and bandleader who has performed over 1,500 concerts in more than 40 countries. As a bandleader, she has appeared at major venues and festivals, including the Kennedy Center, Moscow Symphony Hall, and the Montreal, Newport, and Montreux Jazz Festivals. Early in her career, she performed at Barack Obama’s 2009 Presidential Inauguration and later joined Jon Batiste’s house band on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. She has released 15 albums and is known for a genre-crossing sound blending jazz, pop, and electronic influences.Grace is a nine-time DownBeat Critics Poll Rising Star, winning Alto Saxophone in 2017 and Baritone Saxophone in 2023. As a songwriter, she was awarded “Song of the Year” in the John Lennon Songwriting Contest for Feels Like Home.She has collaborated with artists including Dave Brubeck, Wynton Marsalis, Harry Connick Jr., Gloria Estefan, Lin-Manuel Miranda, and Questlove. She has appeared in film and television, including the Amazon Prime series Bosch, and is an official Yamaha Artist featured in the Emmy Award-winning production The Right Note.An active educator, Grace has taught thousands of students worldwide and is the founder of Sax Pro, an online saxophone community and learning platform. She has held a teaching residency at Berklee College of Music, where she also serves as the youngest member of its Board of Trustees.Ashni is a New York City-based singer, songwriter, and pianist. Weaving jazz, R&B, and pop, with a thread of North Indian folk music, she evokes the incisiveness and soul of Fiona Apple and Hiatus Kaiyote with the genre-crossing, form-expansion of Arooj Aftab. Her work explores our relationship to self, each other, and the natural world, enveloping listeners in a cathartic dimension, providing “haunting relief” (Kajal Mag), and forging a new sound.With over 3.8 million streams and a growing audience, Ashni has captivated sold out rooms at renowned venues like Lincoln Center, Joe’s Pub at The Public Theater, Public Records, Joshua Tree Music Festival, Sunset Sunside in Paris, The Quarter at the Royal Opera House Mumbai, and more.Her music has been featured on Spotify's Women of Jazz playlist, in Ayodele Casel’s Where We Dwell at New York City Center, and the acclaimed, Emmy-nominated web series Brown Girls. She is a member of the Resistance Revival Chorus. Ashni’s EP Who I Dreamed Of released in 2022. Her debut album is set to release in fall 2026. Asian American Arts Alliance is a nonprofit organization dedicated to ensuring greater representation, equity, and opportunities for Asian American artists and cultural organizations through resource sharing, promotion, and community building. A4 serves as a thoughtful convener of the Asian American cultural workforce around issues of race, identity, and artmaking and provides a critical voice for this community. A4 is the only service organization in the country dedicated to the professional development of Asian American artists in all disciplines.Bryant Park Picnic Performances presented by Bank of America is a free outdoor festival that welcomes all New Yorkers to experience the city’s vibrant arts and culture. The series provides a platform for extraordinary artists and serves as a vital outdoor venue for a wide array of New York’s cultural institutions.

events.title: Summer on the Hudson: Climate Film Festival
events.description: Join Riverside Park Conservancy and the Climate Film Festival for a special preview screening of four short films exploring our local environment and the people working to help cities and wildlife adapt to a changing climate. A conversation with filmmakers will follow, including:Emily Driscoll, director, Snow BearsEmily Fano, RiSC, producer, Where It FloodsEliza Mitnick, director, A Fragile ParadiseJason Jaacks, director, Between Moon TidesMaggie Burnette Stogner, director, Refuge KeepersMore to be announced!Snow Bears (2026)Artist Heide Hatry, known as “Snow Banksy,” crafts polar bears out of snow to draw attention to a warming world. What begins as a solitary pandemic project grows into community climate action, as she inspires more than 100 New Yorkers to build snow bears alongside her in Central Park. She dreams of seeing snow bears spread around the globe.Where It Floods: Planting Hope in Coney Island (2023)Where it Floods follows New York City students on the frontline of climate activism in Coney Island as they participate in RiSC, the National Wildlife Federation's award-winning climate education program that connects schools with local residents and partner organizations to help build community resilience.A Fragile Paradise (2026)Beyond its summer crowds and postcard-perfect beaches, Fire Island is sustained by the people who quietly care for it year-round. A Fragile Paradise follows landscaper Dylan Wallace, who helps preserve the island's fragile dunes; Margaret Hofbeck, whose monarch butterfly garden has become a sanctuary for endangered butterflies; and longtime shopkeepers Lynn and Wes Little, whose dockside market has served as the heart of Seaview for generations. Together, their stories reveal the many ways people care for a place, from protecting delicate ecosystems to preserving the traditions and relationships that define a place. Through intimate observational moments and sweeping coastal imagery, A Fragile Paradise is a portrait of Fire Island through the people who sustain it—a reflection on stewardship, resilience, and our relationship to the places we call home.Between Moon Tides (2025)Between Moon Tides follows an intergenerational group of citizen scientists in coastal New England as they attempt to save the Saltmarsh Sparrow from extinction — one nest at a time. Against the backdrop of rising sea levels, three retirees and a young intern forge deep bonds while scouring the saltmarsh, banding birds, and witnessing firsthand the devastating effects of climate change. Through stunning visuals and intimate storytelling, the film reveals how a disappearing bird serves as both a warning and a call to action. Yet, at its heart, Between Moon Tides is a love story—about nature, mentorship, and the hope that comes from refusing to give up, even in the face of impossible odds.Refuge Keepers (2026)Where the sea is both livelihood and legacy, veteran fishermen, women community leaders, and young conservationists unite in Celestún, Mexico to create a pioneering marine refuge, hoping to save the waters that sustain their community and way of life.

events.title: Bryant Park Picnic Performance: Brass Festival: New Breed Brass Band, Aberdeen, and Brass Queens
events.description: Bryant Park's first-ever Brass Festival brings three incredible incredible brass ensembles to the main stage. From Brass Queens' female-led upbeat horns, to Aberdeen's inventive jazz/indie rock blend, and finishing with the New Orleans-born, Grammy-nominated New Breed Brass Band, this high-energy celebration of modern brass is the perfect way to herald in the end of summer. New Breed Brass Band fuses NOLA’s fertile brass band tradition with Caribbean, hip-hop, and modern R&B in the vein of Bruno Mars and Anderson .Paak. The explosive group makes music by and for the Crescent City’s next generation: joyful, vital and unstoppable. New Breed Brass Band is led by drummer Jenard Andrews, son of Tremé trumpet legend James Andrews and nephew of New Orleans scene lynchpin Trombone Shorty. Under Trombone Shorty’s tutelage a new sound was born, and audiences took notice.The band has toured North America and Europe and opened for The Fray, Blackalicious and Dr. John. With the band’s debut album, 2023’s Made In New Orleans, New Breed is hewing a new path for 21st century second-lines, and everyone’s invited to join the procession.Aberdeen is a Brooklyn-based horn band known for its soulful melody-driven instrumental arrangements. Aberdeen's music is about community; a large collective of musicians featuring Allison Philips on trumpet, Olivia Hughart, Jared Yee, Mackenzie McCarthy, Brian Plautz & Stephen Chen on saxes, Jacob Melsha & Jasmi Perales on trombones, Shubh Saran on guitar, Ronnie Lanzilotta on bass and Ross Pederson on drums. Aberdeen's albums Downpour and Held Together showcase their energetic, massive, one-of-a-kind sound.Hailing from Brooklyn, NY, the award-winning Brass Queens are a female-led brass band featuring all-female horns with a sound that sits right at the intersection of the Big Apple and the Big Easy. Their music is deeply inspired by and pays homage to the New Orleans brass band tradition while injecting the upbeat, multifaceted energy of their New York home into each performance. Brass Queens tour regularly across the country and internationally, increasing the visibility of female musicians in the industry.Bryant Park Picnic Performances presented by Bank of America is a free outdoor festival that welcomes all New Yorkers to experience the city’s vibrant arts and culture. The series provides a platform for extraordinary artists and serves as a vital outdoor venue for a wide array of New York’s cultural institutions.

events.title: Trees Count at McKinley Park
events.description: Volunteer with NYC Parks for Trees Count! At each event you will receive a tote bag with all the materials needed to count trees. Returning volunteers are welcome, and will receive additional giveaway items such as shirts, books, and hip bags as supplies last. Next, we'll provide a 30-minute training session that includes the basics of tree identification and how to measure and assess each tree. Using our Tree Census app, you’ll split up into different zones within the park to start counting trees! After completing your first training event, you are welcome to continue counting trees on your own in smaller parks across the city. For your comfort and safety, please bring water and wear closed-toe shoes to this program.

events.title: Wheel Fun Rentals Celebrates America's 250th with Patriotic LED Bike Ride
events.description: Wheel Fun Rentals at Boathouse Row is lighting up summer nights in patriotic style as it celebrates America's 250th anniversary with special Red, White & Blue LED Illuminated Surrey Night Rides. Patriotic Surrey Nights Rides are available now and will run through Labor Day Weekend at their Bensonhurst Park and FDR Boardwalk at Sand Lane bike rental locations.For the summer-long celebration, Wheel Fun Rentals has transformed its popular LED-illuminated specialty bikes into dazzling patriotic attractions featuring custom red, white, and blue lighting. Families, couples, and friends can cruise along two of New York City's scenic waterfronts while celebrating America's historic 250th birthday.On July 4th, guests can make the holiday even more memorable by riding to waterfront viewing areas for spectacular fireworks displays. Launching from Bensonhurst Park in Brooklyn, riders can enjoy the festive atmosphere along the waterfront bike path with views across New York Harbor. On Staten Island, guests can pedal along the FDR Boardwalk, where the waterfront provides a scenic setting to take in the evening's Independence Day celebrations and fireworks over the harbor.Night Rides are first-come, first-served and available Friday – Sundays and holidays beginning at sunset until 10pm, last 1-hour rental goes out at 9pm. Pricing is $29 for a Single Surrey (seats up to 3 adults and 2 small children), and $39 for a Double Surrey (seats up to 6 adults and 2 small children).For additional location information, current hours of operation, and to learn more about Wheel Fun Rentals available recreational rental options, visit wheelfunrentals.com/NYC.

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Wheel Fun Rentals Celebrates America's 250th with Patriotic LED Bike Ride
events.description: Wheel Fun Rentals at Boathouse Row is lighting up summer nights in patriotic style as it celebrates America's 250th anniversary with special Red, White & Blue LED Illuminated Surrey Night Rides. Patriotic Surrey Nights Rides are available now and will run through Labor Day Weekend at their Bensonhurst Park and FDR Boardwalk at Sand Lane bike rental locations.For the summer-long celebration, Wheel Fun Rentals has transformed its popular LED-illuminated specialty bikes into dazzling patriotic attractions featuring custom red, white, and blue lighting. Families, couples, and friends can cruise along two of New York City's scenic waterfronts while celebrating America's historic 250th birthday.On July 4th, guests can make the holiday even more memorable by riding to waterfront viewing areas for spectacular fireworks displays. Launching from Bensonhurst Park in Brooklyn, riders can enjoy the festive atmosphere along the waterfront bike path with views across New York Harbor. On Staten Island, guests can pedal along the FDR Boardwalk, where the waterfront provides a scenic setting to take in the evening's Independence Day celebrations and fireworks over the harbor.Night Rides are first-come, first-served and available Friday – Sundays and holidays beginning at sunset until 10pm, last 1-hour rental goes out at 9pm. Pricing is $29 for a Single Surrey (seats up to 3 adults and 2 small children), and $39 for a Double Surrey (seats up to 6 adults and 2 small children).For additional location information, current hours of operation, and to learn more about Wheel Fun Rentals available recreational rental options, visit wheelfunrentals.com/NYC.

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: "Prior Occupants" Artist Talk & Special Screening with Alison Nguyen
events.description: Join us for the premiere of Alison Nguyen’s new film Prior Occupants, co-commissioned by High Line Art and CHANEL Culture Fund. Following the screening, Nguyen will be joined in conversation by High Line Art Associate Curator, Taylor Zakarin, to discuss her practice and this exciting new work.This event is rain or shine. Although advance RSVP is full, walk-up visitors will be welcome if the event is not at capacity._____________________________________________________________________________________________________Alison Nguyen is a visual artist working across video, installation, performance, and sculpture. Using approaches of speculative fiction, documentary research, and embodied performance, Nguyen creates works that reconsider how narratives operate within the individual, the institution, the archive, and within the politics of cultural memory.In her compelling new film for High Line Originals, co-commissioned with CHANEL Culture Fund, Nguyen explores the obscure nuclear history of Westbeth Artist Housing’s building—the former headquarters for Bell Laboratories, a research facility tied to the development of communication technologies and, later, the atomic bomb. Inspired by a severed fragment of the original High Line freight rail left embedded in Westbeth’s facade, and the High Line’s own history of transformation, Nguyen reflects on the historical narratives that persist—and those quietly erased—within sites of adaptive reuse.Long before Westbeth’s conversion into a historic public housing community for artists in 1970, the site was occupied by Western Electric and later Bell Labs—a crucible of innovation where critical cinema, telecommunications, and military technologies were researched, including components later used in the development of the atomic bomb. Both Bell Labs and Westbeth Artist Housing are places created to pursue large, even utopian ideals. In the case of the former, technological innovation; in the case of the latter government-funded artist housing. Prior Occupants explores what remains of the pursuit of these ideals, how the surrounding architecture has shaped its inhabitants, and the contradictions of present-day Westbeth in the context of the High Line’s surrounding neighborhood.Prior Occupants is an assemblage of audiovisual material including sculpturally re-filmed archival documents, choreographed performance sequences, and layered fragments of audio interviews with the very residents and architects who have shaped Westbeth and the High Line. Through this collage of voices and textures, the artist explores individual and collective relationships to place, technological acceleration, and mortality, and foregrounds the ways in which the structures of the past quietly haunt our future-present. Questioning the relationship between ruination and cultural production, the work asks: What does it mean to stage the decay of an industrial past within public environments and within public artist housing? What role does nature play in these acts of preservation? Nguyen’s film weaves together infrastructure, memory, and technology to consider how the legacy of the nuclear age continues to shape our collective experiences, and positions the High Line not just as a space for leisure, but as an active conduit of our historical consciousness.Part of High Line Channel, High Line Originals is High Line Art’s commissioning program for artists working in time-based media. This initiative invites emerging or underrecognized US-based artists, nominated by a trusted group of contemporary curators, to submit a proposal for a new video work that considers the context of the park in a meaningful way and will resonate with our diverse audience.High Line Originals launched in 2019 with Tourmaline’s Salacia, which is now held in the Museum of Modern Art’s permanent collection. Other past commissions include Onyeka Igwe’s The Miracle on George Green (2021), and Alicia Mersy’s NYC Wisdom (2024). In 2025, High Line Art partnered with CHANEL Culture Fund, and together co-commissioned Frank WANG Yefeng’s Groundless Flower – ? (2025).

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026

events.title: Poetry at Bryant Park Reading Room
events.description: Cai Sherley (he/him) is a Black trans poet-educator with roots in Boston, MA. Cai is a two-time Pushcart Prize nominee, with work published or forthcoming in Best New Poets, swamp pink, Peach Mag, and Tupelo, as well as the anthology I Feel Nothing Like Good: Poets Against Genocide from Taylor & Co Books. His work centers Black transmasculine life, past and present, in the United States, and has found homes at The Watering Hole, Brooklyn Poets, Tin House, LAMBDA, and the Fine Arts Work Center. Cai is a member of the Crossroads Writers Collective and Trans Corner Poets, and the proud stepfather of two sphinxes. He is the author of Out of Yearning, selected by Kay Ulanday Barrett as part of SRP’s 2026 Bridges Series.Charlie Lou Evans (he/they) grew up in a small town in New Jersey, went to college at Virginia Tech, spent two summers thru-hiking the east and west coast, and now lives in Bellingham, Washington. His first chapbook, Gay Sex, celebrates the liberating power of queer love and was released by Sibling Rivalry Press this June. He explores gender and sexuality through poetry and finds it most fulfilling when others see themselves in their work.JC Andrews (she/her) is a lesbian poet from Springfield, Arkansas. Her work can be found in Gulf Coast, The Massachusetts Review, Waxwing, and elsewhere. Her debut collection, Of an Ilk, was a finalist for the 2024 National Poetry Series and won the 2026 Yale Series of Younger Poets competition. It will be published with Yale University Press in April 2027. Her chapbook, Trillion Amber Trumpets, was published with Sibling Rivalry Press in April 2026 as part of the Arkansas Queer Poet Series.Kaitlin Hsu ?? (she/her/?) is a queer Taiwanese poet who believes in a free Palestine. A 2025 Lambda Literary Fellow and 2024 Margins Fellow at the Asian American Writers Workshop, she has also received support from Brooklyn Poets, genARTS Silicon Valley, the Mendocino Coast Writers Conference, and more. She is the author of the chapbook Paper Dolls (Sibling Rivalry Press), selected by Kay Ulanday Barrett as part of SRP’s 2026 Bridges Series. Her work can be found most recently in A Public Space, Poet Lore, and Peach Mag. She currently works at Kaya Press as an associate editor and development coordinator.Toni Garcia-Butler (he/they) is a poet and community artist-educator rooted in Little Rock, Arkansas. He approaches his craft as a memory keeper, believing that poets and artists can be creative cultural archivists. His writing and art center the lived experiences of his people: Black, Fil-am, southern, trans/queer, and everyone existing within the intersections. As a facilitator, Toni encourages folks to empower themselves through DIY publishing/zinemaking, personal narrative, and creative joy. In 2025, Toni was named Best Poet in Arkansas by the Arkansas Times. His chapbook, D I Y Body, was published with Sibling Rivalry Press in June 2026 as part of the Arkansas Queer Poet Series.Hosted by:Bryan Borland is the founding publisher of Sibling Rivalry Press and founding editor of Assaracus: A Journal of Gay and Queer Poetry. He is the author of multiple poetry collections, including Brotherful, a finalist for the Thom Gunn Award for Gay Poetry, and DIG, a finalist for the Lambda Literary Award in Gay Poetry and Stonewall Honor Book as honored by the American Library Association. His most recent book is Listen, Kid: Selected and New Poems (2010-2026).Kay Ulanday Barrett is a poet, essayist, and cultural strategist. Barrett is a 2024 Disabled Futures fellow awarded by The Ford Foundation, Mellon Foundation, and United States Artists. They are the winner of the 2022 Foundation for Contemporary Arts Cy Twombly Award for Poetry, a winner of the 2022 Next Book Residency with Tin House, a James Baldwin Fellowship at MacDowell, residencies at Baldwin for the Arts, and Millay Arts awarded by Lambda Literary. Their second book, More Than Organs (Sibling Rivalry Press, 2020) received a 2021 Stonewall Honor Book Award by the American Library Association and was a Lambda Literary Award Finalist. They have featured at the United Nations, Lincoln Center, Hemispheric Institute, The Whitney, MoMA, Symphony Space, the Ford Foundation, Brooklyn Museum, Princeton, Columbia, Yale, Manchester PRIDE, Sesame Street, & more.

events.description: This workshop offers immigrant families and community members practical information about their legal rights, a broad overview of how the U.S. immigration system operates, and how to prepare for immigration-related emergencies. events.title: Project Evergreen at Phoenix Community Garden Volunteer Workday
events.description: The Phoenix Community Garden in Brooklyn is 1/2 acre of green goodness in the Ocean Hill/Brownsville section of Brooklyn. Phoenix gardeners have changed a formerly vacant lot into a pastoral space where community members come together to make their garden grow. The garden is open to all members of the community. events.description: Solo and group exhibitions at Glyndor Gallery explore the dynamic relationships between nature, culture, and site.
